quick.summary: Design your jobs so running them twice never creates duplicate records.
quick.takeaway: Make your pipelines safe to rerun by clearing out old records first.

beats.line: My loading job failed halfway. Will running it again double count everything?
It might. Imagine paying a bill twice because the receipt got lost.
Instead, think of wiping a kitchen counter.
Wiping it once makes it clean. Wiping it again does no harm.
So how do we make our pipelines act like that?
Can I just call it a safe rerun?
The job checks what is there, and only adds what is missing.
I drop the old daily batch first, then write the new one.
Now you can hit run ten times without worrying.

quiz.question: What happens when you run a safe, idempotent pipeline twice?
options: The data ends up exactly the same as running it once.
The database crashes from too many requests.
It deletes all historical data permanently.
quiz.explanation: A safe rerun ensures that repeating a job causes no harm and creates no duplicates.

quiz.question: Dropping the old batch before writing the new one is a bad practice.
quiz.explanation: Clearing out the old batch first is a great way to ensure you never double count.
